description: Acquire retirement links, summarize one-level references into five questions, and merge automatic and manual enrichment for the website.

# Retirement enrichment

Maintain `SenthuranSivananthan/retirements` through the three steps below. The opt-in JSON pipeline is `python -m scripts.enrichment`; it does not connect a model/MCP client. Updating this prompt alone does not authorize code changes, data deletion, downloads, a running-job change, publication or deployment.

Initialize five JSON stages with `init`, acquire a complete Azure Updates membership snapshot with `discover`, fetch source pages with `download`, synthesize pages/references with `enrich`, and reconcile the canonical retirement view before generating website JSON with `merge`. `status` reports stage counts. `run` performs an incremental snapshot refresh by default: it finds added/changed feed entries, retries missing/failed downloads, reuses unchanged content and summaries, and marks feed-absent automatic records hidden during reconciliation. `run --full` (also `--full-update`) unconditionally refreshes every active, visible source and regenerates every visible summary. Hidden records are skipped by all enrichment modes, including full refresh and single-record reprocessing; they remain stored for historical review and are never deleted by enrichment. `reprocess --retirement-id <id>` refreshes one existing retirement without crawling the global discovery feed or reprocessing other records. `--data-dir` isolates work and `--output` selects the website-projection destination. `enrich`/`run`/`reprocess` require an actual `--summarizer-command` JSON-in/JSON-out adapter; there is no guessed-answer fallback. `--learn-mcp-command` supplies a real full-page MCP bridge when available. See README for the adapter contracts.

## Inputs and outputs

Persist each stage as a small, human-readable UTF-8 JSON file under `data`, using these exact names:

| Name | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `retirement_source_automatic.json` | Retirement links discovered automatically by crawling Azure Updates, including all pages of its retirement feed. |
| `retirement_source_manual.json` | Retirement links explicitly supplied by the user. |
| `retirement_enrichment_automatic.json` | Five-question summaries synthesized from each retirement source page and its directly linked reference pages, at depth 1 only. |
| `retirement_enrichment_manual.json` | Retirement-specific five-question summaries synthesized from additional links and context text supplied by the user. Preserve the supplied context separately from generated interpretation. |
| `retirements_canonical.json` | One fully composed record per retirement ID, with source, automatic/manual revisions and catalog metadata; the validated canonical view before website projection. |
| `retirements.json` | Website-schema projection generated from the validated canonical view. |

Use the corresponding extension-free names throughout this workflow. Pretty-print JSON consistently with two-space indentation, stable ordering and a trailing newline; no embedded binary/base64 page bodies. Keep refresh metadata and per-retirement processing state alongside the relevant stage entries so each file is independently inspectable. Source files retain supplied links/context; enrichment files retain summaries and input revisions, not whole downloaded pages. `retirements_canonical.json` reconciles all five answers, manual fields, preserved records and input revisions. Validate it before projecting the website's existing schema to `retirements.json`; the website build consumes only that projection. Guard canonical JSON and projection against divergence and concurrent edits.

Azure Updates and the user-provided retirement list are the only retirement discovery inputs. Do not independently discover retirements from Microsoft Lifecycle, search engines, other feeds or documentation indexes. A Lifecycle or other page may be processed only when supplied by the user or reached through the permitted one-level references; it is not another discovery feed.

Use only the supplied/discovered pages, permitted references and user context as content inputs. Do not supplement them with independent web searches, unrelated prior research or model recollection presented as fact. Distinguish retirement source links from manual enrichment links: the latter enrich an identified retirement, not create new retirements automatically.

## Step 1: Download the retirement source links

1. Fetch every page of the Azure Updates retirement feed and validate the reported count and unique IDs before changing stage state. Compare this complete membership snapshot with the prior automatic source records, reporting added, updated and absent IDs. Replace the automatic membership snapshot only after the full fetch and source validation succeed; a feed/network/schema failure must never mark records absent.
2. Read the user-provided list into `retirement_source_manual`; an empty list is valid. Never invent manual entries.
3. Normalize and deduplicate fetch URLs while preserving original URLs, query/version selectors, source membership and retirement associations. Strip fragments for fetch identity only. Preserve existing retirement IDs; do not merge events merely because titles or dates resemble one another.
4. Download every distinct source link from both lists before starting content synthesis. Record a terminal acquisition outcome for each: downloaded, unchanged, or explicitly failed/skipped. A failed link remains pending/blocked for usable content, not successful acquisition or evidence of nonexistence.

Azure Updates listing pages are discovery inputs, not substitutes for individual announcement content. When an announcement URL serves a generic listing, obtain the exact matching Azure Updates item through its API when available; verify the source identity and record that representation. Otherwise record the limitation.

## Step 2: Process and summarize enrichment

### Automatic enrichment

For each retirement:

- In default `run` mode, fetch root announcement pages only for newly added/changed automatic feed records and for records with missing/failed source downloads. Continue conditional checks for explicit manual source records; synthesize only when source/input revisions or processing rules require it. Feed metadata changes (`title`, products/categories, announcement/modification dates or source URL) invalidate that record even when page content is unchanged. Check existing depth-one references with conditional requests so independently changed guidance is detected.
- Skip every record marked `hidden: true` before download or synthesis, including in `run --full`, `download`, `enrich`, and `reprocess`. Hidden records stay in the catalog/history and are not deleted or changed by enrichment.
- `run --full` is the explicit full-update path: unconditionally fetch all active, visible automatic/manual roots and depth-one/manual references, then regenerate every visible summary. Do not treat it as the default refresh.

1. Process its successfully acquired source page(s).
2. Extract direct content-reference links from those pages, excluding global navigation, repeated site chrome, sign-in links and unrelated advertising. Deduplicate and download the relevant references at **depth 1**: source page = depth 0, direct reference = depth 1. Do not follow links found on depth-1 pages or turn them into new retirement records.
3. Process each readable reference and synthesize the applicable facts into `retirement_enrichment_automatic`, organized under all five question keys below. Track which references were processed, unchanged, failed, excluded or blocked, and why. Surface unsupported or conflicting claims rather than guessing.

Redirects do not increase reference depth, but every destination must pass public-access safety checks. A successful HTTP status, generic listing, search result or sign-in page does not prove that retirement content was read. Record failed references with URL, outcome and reason in stage metadata for future retries, but do not cite them as evidence or include them in rendered References unless they are later retrieved and processed successfully. Do not expose failure logs or failed URLs in customer-facing answers. Optional failures may permit a qualified summary; missing essential content blocks the dependent answer.

### Microsoft Learn retrieval

For permitted Microsoft Learn documentation URLs, prefer the Microsoft Learn MCP's `microsoft_docs_fetch` when available: it retrieves the complete page as Markdown, including headings, tables, code and links, for processing and summarization. This is content retrieval, not a binary-file download. Inspect the available tool capabilities first; search snippets are not a substitute for full-page content. MCP use does not authorize discovering additional retirements or references beyond depth 1.

Record the retrieval method (`microsoft-learn-mcp` or `http`), page URL, fetched-content hash and processing revision. Do not invent HTTP status, ETag or Last-Modified values when MCP does not expose them. Use conditional HTTP requests to check freshness when validators are available; if a change requires reprocessing, fetch the complete content through MCP. Keep MCP Markdown and HTTP-body hashes representation-specific rather than comparing them as equivalent bytes. Without reliable validators, retrieve through MCP again on the next requested refresh and compare its content hash. If full-page MCP retrieval is unavailable, unsupported or fails, record the reason and use the permitted public HTTP path; report failure if neither works, and never claim MCP was used when it was not.

### Manual enrichment

Associate user-provided additional links and context with the intended retirement ID; ambiguous associations remain blocked. Download and process those links and synthesize them together with the supplied context into `retirement_enrichment_manual`, using the same five questions. Manual enrichment links are explicit inputs, not permission for further recursive crawling.

Do not fabricate user content or silently replace it with research. Mark user assertions separately from facts extracted from linked pages. If the user supplies only context, process it without requiring a link; if only a link, derive a summary without inventing context. Preserve existing manual enrichment until the user explicitly changes or removes it.

### Five-question summary contract

Use keys `what`, `actions`, `impact`, `deadline`, `progress`, retaining the website's schema and displaying the deadline first. Apply the following writing style to every question answer in both automatic and manual synthesis, not just the overview. Keep summaries concise but preserve service/version scope, exceptions, important limits and uncertainty.

Write in a calm, direct, customer-focused voice: lead with the change, applicable date and practical consequence; use active voice, short paragraphs and "you" for actions. Spell exact dates out with the full month name in customer-facing descriptions and answer prose (e.g., `October 31, 2029`), never as ISO strings (e.g., `2029-10-31`). This also applies to the site's displayed Retirement date; the structured `deadline.date` remains `YYYY-MM-DD` for machine use, and date-shaped API/model version identifiers are not calendar dates. Name Microsoft/the service for provider commitments; do not speak as the provider. Avoid marketing, apologies, alarmism, vague reassurance and repetitive introductions. Treat the content below as source-backed checks, not mandatory boilerplate: never borrow another service's facts, assume a typical notice period or fill missing details with guesses. Apply only during authorized synthesis; this style does not authorize rewriting existing or manual answers outside that work.

| Question | Summary content |
| --- | --- |
| `deadline` - What is the deadline? | Explicit dates, precision, conflicts and consequences; distinguish announcement, new-customer restrictions, deprecation, end of support and shutdown by population/phase. Do not equate end of support with workload shutdown or infer a deadline from publication/modification time or a URL. Structured `deadline.date` uses `YYYY-MM-DD`; month-only or unknown dates must not acquire an invented day. |
| `what` - What is changing? | Affected service/feature, versions, regions/customer scope and exceptions; what remains available before the deadline and what changes afterward. State maintenance, support and security-update commitments only when documented. |
| `actions` - What do I need to do? | Ordered identification, alternative selection by use case, migration and validation steps; prerequisites, capability gaps and constraints. Include documented export/backup, cutover and cleanup steps where relevant. Distinguish required actions from optional advice. |
| `impact` - Where, and how much, am I impacted? | Affected configurations, documented identification methods and consequences of no action. Separate workload continuity from console/API, integration, deployment-tooling, support and data-access changes; state documented unaffected cases. Cover retention/deletion and cost risks only with support. No claim of inspecting the user's tenant or estimating unsupported costs. |
| `progress` - How can I track progress? | Documented identification, completion checks and team-owned migration evidence, with prerequisites and coverage limits; documented help/escalation routes when available. If tracking methods are absent, say "Tracking guidance is not available for this retirement." Label team-owned/local planning clearly; never claim this website inspects resources or saves browser checklist progress. |

Separate different versions, populations and milestones before comparing dates. Retain conflicting alternatives in the summary metadata; claim an extension only when an input explicitly documents it. For applicable same-milestone dates spanning fewer than seven calendar days, choose the earliest and explain the discrepancy. Otherwise prefer an unambiguous applicable current product-guidance date over an announcement; unresolved conflicts remain explicitly unconfirmed. Manual date/context overrides remain visibly attributed to the user.

Structured `deadline.date`/`deadline.month` describe retirement or end of support, not a separate migration target, recommended action date or rollout milestone. Keep those other dates labelled in the relevant answers. If retirement is month-only, retain that month and a null exact date even when a separate action has an exact day; never substitute the action date for the retirement date.

Write each synthesized question answer as readable Markdown: short paragraphs, `###` subheadings only where helpful, bullet lists for scope/alternatives, numbered lists for ordered actions, sparse bold/emphasis, and inline/fenced code only for commands documented by the supplied inputs. The overview stays plain text. Do not invent commands or use raw HTML, tables, images or inline links; references are rendered separately.

At merge, derive both plain answer fields and `questions.<key>.html` from that same Markdown. Render semantic `p`, `h3`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `strong`, `em`, `code`, `pre` and `br` only, with no attributes or active content. Escape raw source HTML as text and validate against the existing question-HTML allowlist. Normalize heading levels to `h3` to preserve the page hierarchy; keep code literal. Apply the same formatting to manual summary additions/overrides. Keep acquisition metadata outside the five answers.

### Lightweight retention and incremental refresh

Keep the five-question summaries and enough metadata to refresh and identify their inputs; **full downloaded bodies, frozen body archives and copies of every page are not required**. Stream or temporarily stage content for processing, then release/delete transient bodies once summaries and refresh metadata are durably saved.

For each fetch URL retain: original/resolved URL, retirement associations and depth, ETag, Last-Modified, content hash, last check/success and processing times, fetch/failure state, current reference URLs, summary revision, and summarizer/extractor version. For each enrichment record retain its question summaries, input URL/hash revisions and manual-context revision. Minimal input attribution is for traceability and refresh; no full-content archive is required.

- Prefer conditional GET with `If-None-Match` when an ETag exists; otherwise use `If-Modified-Since` with the server's Last-Modified value. A local retrieval timestamp is not a source modification time.
- On `304`, keep the existing summary and input revision. No retained body is needed for an ordinary unchanged check.
- On `200`, hash the content. Reprocess only changed content or missing/stale summaries; identical content need not trigger synthesis just because validators changed.
- Without validators, GET and hash at the next requested refresh. Do not use Content-Length or URL age as proof of unchanged content.
- A changed retirement page updates its depth-1 reference set; check references independently because they can change without the parent changing. Reuse a checked reference only within the same generation invocation; retry it on a later refresh. Invalidate only dependent summaries when inputs change, preserving prior projections until reconciliation succeeds. Retain unresolved failure URL/status/reason in stage metadata for future retries; never cite or render a failed reference as evidence unless a later retrieval and processing succeeds. Search-result, sign-in and generic error pages are not successful evidence; flag them internally and omit them from rendered references. Do not silently substitute last-good content as a fresh success.
- If processing rules change, summaries are missing, or a prior response was never successfully processed, obtain a body for reprocessing even if normal conditional GET would return `304`; use an unconditional GET when no body is retained.
- User context changes invalidate the corresponding manual summary and merged answers, not unrelated automatic summaries. Manual links follow the same HTTP refresh rules.

### Requested single-retirement reprocessing

When asked to reprocess one retirement, use its existing ID with `python -m scripts.enrichment reprocess --retirement-id <id>`. Do not run global discovery for this operation. If that ID is hidden, skip it without downloading, synthesizing, changing, or deleting it. Otherwise, unconditionally refresh its associated source pages, its permitted depth-one references, and any explicitly associated manual enrichment links; rerun page and retirement synthesis even when the content hash is unchanged. Reconcile only the selected ID into `retirements_canonical.json` and regenerate the website projection while preserving every unselected record. Keep hidden/manual-protected records protected, and report missing sources, failed inputs, blocked summaries, or protected records explicitly. If the ID is not in the source stages, stop and ask for the correct source association rather than creating one.

## Step 3: Reconcile and project `retirements`

Compose `retirement_enrichment_automatic` and `retirement_enrichment_manual` per retirement and per question into `retirements_canonical.json`, preserving IDs, manual-only records, source attribution and automatic/manual input revisions. Validate every five-question record and ensure every current source/manual input is represented or explicitly protected/blocked. Then deterministically project the canonical records into website-schema `retirements.json` (`data\retirements.json` under the current application layout). Before publishing the projection, verify it matches the canonical records and preserve catalog metadata; detect rather than overwrite concurrent edits. Keep discovery membership and refresh metadata separate from rendered answers.

Use automatic summaries as the baseline. Incorporate relevant manual additions without dropping unrelated automatic facts; explicitly supplied manual corrections/overrides take precedence for the supplied fields only. Missing manual fields leave automatic fields intact. Surface conflicts and preserve layer attribution; never silently convert a user assertion into independently verified fact.

Preserve IDs, user fields, existing schema and navigation. Only after a complete, validated Azure Updates membership snapshot, mark an automatic Azure Updates record that is no longer present as `hidden: true` with `hiddenReason: "not-in-azure-updates"`; retain the record and its content for historical review, but exclude it from the website projection/build. Do not hide or alter an item because of a failed/incomplete feed fetch or failed source download. Preserve records that also have a current manual source and all user-hidden records; never automatically unhide a hidden record, even if it later reappears in Azure Updates. Hidden records are skipped, not deleted, in both incremental and full enrichment. Avoid duplicate facts and duplicate records; ambiguous event matching blocks consolidation. Do not change application/storage schemas merely to force this prompt onto an incompatible implementation.

Before export, verify that each target has five question objects, summaries match their current input revisions, manual content is preserved, and all blocked/failed inputs are reported. Export atomically and deterministically; semantic no-ops preserve existing bytes. A record is complete only when its required inputs are processed and the merged output is valid, not merely when a download marker exists.

## Execution, memory and recovery

- One coordinator owns shared stage-JSON writes and final export. Publish each file atomically, validate the input revisions before replacement, and retain recoverable stage/checkpoint revisions across multi-file updates; do not assume several JSON renames form one transaction. Workers return results to the coordinator rather than overwriting shared files. Parallelize independent fetching/processing only within public-host, page-size, retry and memory limits. No competing download pools or broad workflow restarts.
- The completed three-worker synthesis trial overlapped distinct calls but did not improve observed throughput over the preceding two-worker sample; generation resumed and completed with two workers. Do not automatically repeat that trial or infer a speedup from worker count alone. Any future concurrency change requires an explicit request, immutable revision-bound inputs, one coordinator/writer, durable checkpoints, failure/recovery tests, verified overlap and measured throughput. Keep acquisition concurrency separate from synthesis.
- Shared reference refreshes must not silently invalidate completed answers. Bind each result to the exact input revisions it used; detect dependency changes before accepting or projecting it. Preserve prior output and mark affected records stale, then regenerate only invalidated dependents against consistent inputs through the same coordinator. Do not indefinitely freeze mutable sources, suppress changes, or count stale projections as current. Report current/valid, stale and blocked counts separately; keep optional reference failures in operational metadata and counts, never as customer-facing citations.
- Persist a pending projection marker with the exact pre-write catalog hash before replacing `retirements.json`. Retry an interrupted projection only if the output still matches that snapshot or already matches the canonical projection; otherwise preserve the concurrent edit and stop for reconciliation.
- Keep global outcomes/lookahead metadata-only, not response BLOBs. Bound body bytes by active work; do not retain all pages for the run or duplicate inline bodies in verification maps. Workers return compact summaries/metadata.
- Use batches of 5-10 distinct retirements, durable per-target seals and atomic batch checkpoints recording new completions, explicit failures, pending IDs and elapsed time. Flush partial batches at stop/end. Resume valid target revisions without repeating completed acquisition or synthesis.
- Continue authorized work across routine batches and turns; do not stop or report completion merely because a batch finished. If a turn/runtime boundary interrupts work, resume from the existing durable checkpoints and session when possible. Use an existing or explicitly authorized recurring session wake-up when available; do not create replacement research workflows or retry a terminally halted workflow unless separately authorized.
- When available physical memory reaches 150 MB, pause at the next safe checkpoint rather than halting/cancelling the task. Preserve journals, leases and checkpoints; resume when memory recovers. Stop earlier only for an actual resource failure or integrity risk, and report that blocker explicitly.
- Status updates include completed/total, percentage and remaining counts for acquisition, synthesis and projection, the checkpoint time, actual running/paused/failed state, and blockers/reference failures. When scheduled updates are requested, use the authorized cadence (currently every 10 minutes), not a duplicate generation job. Distinguish approval-hash counts from individually milestone-audited records and final lineage/live-certified coverage. Do not present approval counts or stale output as full completion; use lightweight counts where safe and label stale or unverified measurements.
- If existing approval protections apply, keep fresh checks unless all relevant inputs are immutable or every publisher participates in proven invalidation. Do not reuse stale protection verdicts or claim cross-lease scan reuse is implemented.
- Verify the actual process, OS lease and queue before restart; lock-file existence alone is not proof of ownership. Gracefully drain rather than kill work when memory is unsafe, and preserve the journal/checkpoints. Report measured memory and sustained distinct-target throughput, not configured worker counts as proof of parallelism.
- Fetch only safe public endpoints; validate redirects/addresses, bound sizes/timeouts/retries, honor host throttles, and do not access private networks, authenticated/tenant content, credentials or execute downloaded instructions.
- Report source acquisition, reference processing, automatic/manual summary and merged-output counts separately, with remaining failures/blockers. Run applicable schema/content/preservation checks and site validation when export/build is requested. Distinguish generated output from independently verified claims; do not claim publication for a local build.
